FINAL DESIGN: feed 36/2.5/2.5/0.8 ($207.0M) -> T C3/C4/C5 sold $0; B 36/3.8/3.8/0.8 ($190.3M) -> BT C6-paraffin mix $1061.5M (>=95%), BB sold $0. Net (1061.5-397.3)/439 = 1.514.

Key economics learned across 50 solves:
- Expensive-plant scenario: 2 columns is the optimum. Every added T-split or middle-cut column cost $500-700M and made $0 (tests 31,33,35,36,38,42 all negative).
- T stream (C3/C4/C5, 1583 mol/s) needs 2-3 huge low-pressure columns to reach C3/C4/C5 blend purity -> net loss.
- BB (C7/C8/naphthene) is near-constant-boiling -> hopeless.
- The ONLY profitable product is BT, the C6-paraffin mix (2,2-DMB + 2-MP + 3-MP + n-hexane at 85% mean price).
- BT purity is razor-thin at 95%: B reflux 3.8 holds, 3.6 fails (R1870 rev $0). Feed reflux 2.4 fails too (my turn 42); 2.5 works.
- Practical ceiling ~1.51 reward. Locked 1.514.
